headline: 3 Zero-Server Utilities You Can Build This Weekend
summary: Discover three practical serverless utilities that run entirely on edge platforms like Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, and Deno Deploy. No servers to manage, infinite scale, and deployable in minutes.

slides.eyebrow: SERVERLESS PLATFORMS (CLOUDFLARE WORKERS, VERCEL EDGE, DENO DEPLOY) UPDATE
slides.title: Tired of Managing Servers for Tiny Tools?
slides.subtitle: Build useful utilities that run globally with zero infrastructure.
slides.body: Every developer has ideas for small tools — URL shorteners, webhook catchers, API proxies — but spinning up a server feels like overkill. What if you could deploy them in minutes, pay nothing at idle, and scale automatically?
slides.deep_dive: Traditional hosting requires provisioning VMs, configuring load balancers, managing SSL certificates, and paying for idle capacity. Edge serverless platforms eliminate all of this by running your code directly in globally distributed data centers, invoked only when requests arrive. This shifts the mental model from 'managing servers' to 'writing request handlers.'
slides.key_fact: Edge functions execute in milliseconds cold-start, not seconds.
slides.why_it_matters: Removes infrastructure friction so you can ship weekend ideas to production users instantly.

slides.title: Three Utilities, Three Platforms, Zero Servers
slides.subtitle: Each utility showcases a different edge platform strength.
slides.body: Utility 1: Smart URL shortener with analytics on Cloudflare Workers. Utility 2: Webhook receiver with replay on Vercel Edge. Utility 3: API aggregator proxy on Deno Deploy. All deploy via CLI in under a minute.
slides.deep_dive: Cloudflare Workers excels at KV storage and durable objects for stateful edge logic. Vercel Edge integrates natively with Next.js middleware and offers seamless preview deployments. Deno Deploy provides first-class TypeScript support, standard library compatibility, and built-in testing. Each platform handles TLS, routing, and global distribution automatically.
slides.key_fact: No Docker, no Kubernetes, no cloud console clicking required.
slides.why_it_matters: Match the utility to the platform's superpower for optimal developer experience.

slides.title: How Edge Functions Handle Requests
slides.subtitle: Request hits nearest POP → isolates spins up → code runs → response returns.
slides.body: Your handler receives a standard Request object, processes it, and returns a Response. The platform manages isolation, scaling, and routing transparently.
slides.deep_dive: When a request arrives at the nearest point of presence, the platform either reuses a warm isolate or spins up a new V8 isolate (milliseconds). Your code executes with access to platform APIs: KV storage, caches, environment variables, and fetch. No Node.js process, no Express server — just a fetch event handler. The isolate terminates after response or CPU limit.
slides.key_fact: Isolates provide multi-tenancy without container overhead.
slides.why_it_matters: Understanding isolate lifecycle helps you design stateless, fast handlers.

slides.title: Edge Utility Architecture Pattern
slides.subtitle: Minimal components, maximum distribution.
slides.body: Code lives in Git → CI/CD pushes to edge → global network serves requests → logs stream to dashboard.
slides.deep_dive: The architecture eliminates traditional tiers. Your handler is the API, the edge network is the load balancer, KV/Durable Objects replace databases for simple state, and the platform dashboard replaces monitoring stack. Git push triggers deployment to hundreds of locations simultaneously. Rollback is instant. Preview URLs generate per PR.
slides.key_fact: Single deploy command propagates to 300+ locations globally.
slides.why_it_matters: Architecture complexity drops from O(n) services to O(1) handler file.

slides.title: Developer Workflow: Idea to Global Endpoint
slides.subtitle: Write → Test locally → Deploy → Share URL.
slides.body: Local emulator mirrors production. One command deploys. Preview URLs for every branch. Zero config for custom domains.
slides.deep_dive: Each platform provides a local development server that mimics edge runtime: same APIs, same limits, same behavior. You write TypeScript, test with curl or browser, then deploy. The CLI handles bundling, minification, and upload. Environment secrets sync securely. Custom domains map via CNAME. Analytics appear in dashboard within seconds.
slides.key_fact: Local emulator runs identical V8 isolate as production.
slides.why_it_matters: No surprise bugs from environment differences; confidence in every deploy.

slides.output: Global HTTPS endpoint + preview URLs + analytics dashboard

slides.title: Edge Constraints That Bite Beginners
slides.subtitle: CPU time limits, no filesystem, cold starts on free tiers.
slides.body: Avoid long computations. Use streaming for large responses. Store state in KV, not memory. Batch external calls.
slides.deep_dive: Edge runtimes enforce strict CPU limits (typically 10-50ms on free tiers). No Node.js built-ins like fs, path, or child_process. Global variables reset per isolate. Cold starts add latency on free plans after inactivity. KV writes are eventually consistent. Durable Objects serialize access per key. Design for stateless, fast, parallelizable work.
slides.key_fact: Free tiers include millions of requests monthly across all three platforms.
slides.why_it_matters: Respecting constraints prevents timeout errors and unexpected bills.
items: Don't run heavy loops — offload to queues or background workers
Don't assume in-memory state persists — use KV or Durable Objects
Don't block on sequential fetches — use Promise.all for parallel calls
Don't ignore CPU limits — profile locally with platform emulator
Do stream large responses — avoids buffering limits
Do use edge caching headers — reduces origin load dramatically

slides.title: Deploy Your First Utility Tonight
slides.subtitle: Pick a platform, run one command, share a working URL.
slides.body: Cloudflare: npm create cloudflare@latest. Vercel: npx vercel. Deno: deno deploy. All free to start.
slides.deep_dive: Each platform's CLI scaffolds a starter project with TypeScript config, local dev server, and deploy script. Cloudflare Wrangler creates workers with KV bindings. Vercel CLI links to Git for auto-deploys. Deno Deploy imports directly from GitHub. Documentation includes templates for URL shorteners, webhook handlers, and API proxies. Community Discord servers offer instant help.
slides.key_fact: Zero credit card required for generous free tiers on all three.
slides.why_it_matters: Zero friction from idea to production — the ultimate developer velocity.
takeaways: Install one CLI tonight and deploy a hello-world edge function
Build a URL shortener with Cloudflare Workers + KV this weekend
Share your endpoint and watch global requests hit your dashboard
